title: Professional R Project Workflow
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of professional r project workflow and identify its main inputs, outputs or constraints.
Apply clarifying the analytical objective in a minimal example and state the expected result before checking it.
Test one relevant edge, missing or failure case and describe a limitation of the result.

content.intro: Professional R Project Workflow is part of Security, Deployment, and Professional Practice. Start with clarifying the analytical objective and connect it to the worked example and expected result.

content_blocks.title: Why this matters
content_blocks.text: Professional R Project Workflow is one step in Security, Deployment, and Professional Practice; production readiness includes more than a successful local script: dependencies, permissions, observability, recovery and privacy matter. The example is intentionally small so you can predict its result before checking it in a local R session.

items.text: Build the smallest example for building modular functions, inspect the returned object, and confirm its names, type and shape before using it downstream.

items.title: Testing and Reviewing Results
items.text: Turn testing and reviewing results into a check with a clear condition, expected result and an example that should fail.

items.title: Reporting and Delivering Outputs

items.title: Maintaining the Project Over Time
items.text: For maintaining the project over time, parse values to a date-time class first and verify formats, timezone assumptions and a boundary date.

content_blocks.title: Work through it
content_blocks.text: Avoid secrets in code, document provenance, test release artifacts, and establish safe rollback and support procedures. Change one input or condition at a time, compare the observed result with your prediction, and write down one limitation.

content_blocks.title: R example: Professional R Project Workflow
content_blocks.code:
checks <- c("no secrets in logs", "validated input", "reviewed output")
length(checks)
content_blocks.run_instructions: CodeLeaf does not provide an R runtime. This block is an inspectable reference example; execute it in a local R console or a reviewed R-aware environment. Static validation checks file structure, not R semantics.
content_blocks.reset_steps: No example is executed by this CodeLeaf lesson. For a local run, use synthetic data in a temporary working directory, avoid production credentials or destructive writes, and restart a clean R session to clear lesson objects.
content_blocks.limitations: Security review should include secrets, data handling, dependencies and output exposure. Verify the snippet and expected output with the supported R and package versions before publishing.

content_blocks.title: Common pitfall
content_blocks.text: Do not treat a syntactically plausible example as proof of correctness. For professional r project workflow, check the input type, missing/empty cases, output shape, and domain assumptions.

content.task: Apply professional r project workflow to a small synthetic example. State the expected result before running the example.

hints: Start with “Clarifying the Analytical Objective” and identify the input and output before coding.
Use synthetic data and explicit validation; do not access production systems or expose credentials.
Test a boundary, missing, invalid or failure input relevant to this topic.

common_mistakes.problem: Using an example without checking its inputs or output shape.
common_mistakes.why: R can coerce types, propagate missing values or simplify results unexpectedly.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect with str(), class(), typeof(), length() or dim() and add a direct check.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating a demonstration as proof that every edge case works.
common_mistakes.why: Empty input, missing values, dependencies and version differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Test a normal case and a boundary/failure case in a clean local R session.

common_mistakes.why: The conclusion depends on data provenance, transformations and assumptions.
common_mistakes.fix: Record input source, cleaning choices and known limitations beside the result.
